The app and exchange? Quite solid, really—clean interface, functional, and undoubtedly reliable. It’s a well-known name, trusted by many, and the app performs robustly. But then there’s that 24-hour cooling-off period for new users.

Now, I get it—regulations are important, and no one’s keen on pandemonium in the trading world. But honestly, locking users out for 24 hours feels a bit excessive. It’s as if you’ve assumed we’ve already made some catastrophic mistake before we’ve even touched the “Buy” button. A tad dramatic, don’t you think?

Why not just hand us a consent form instead? Something where we tick a box to declare we’re either grizzled veterans of the trading floor or nervous newbies who may, indeed, need 24 hours to cool our jets. Let us decide if we want to be “babysat,” rather than imposing this one-size-fits-all timeout.

Because, let’s face it, 24 hours in the trading world is practically a lifetime. That’s long enough to miss a golden buying opportunity or two, stew over our lost chances, and possibly compose a scathing review—like this one.

For those who don’t know, cfds are otc (over the counter) leveraged derivatives and your broker takes the other side of the trade. Naturally you profiting means they need to pay you even if their entire clientele takes the same side of the trade and it turns out to be a winner. A message came up displaying “You can place market orders after the instrument receives a new price. Pending orders are still accepted”. Not even allowing me to close my overnight positions that were in the opposite direction. Not only did I miss out on the opportunity to make a couple quid, I lost more than I would have if only i had been allowed to close my trade. Further more i see real time price differences for identical assets in the stocks and shares account and the cfd account. This broker doesn’t want you to win.
